subject: RF plot is showing some noise

messages.author: 37bf83ea6e1bb5bb
messages.subject: RF plot is showing some noise
parts:
Dear All,

I plotted RF plot in my data set. most of the SNPs are plotted away from diagonal.  Does it make any noise during construction of the genetic map? 

Regards
Gilly

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] RF plot is showing some noise
parts:
Seems you've got some problems with marker placement, that markers on chr 1 are linked to markers on 11, and 2/12, 3/13, ..., 9/19.

karl

It can happen in the case of polyploid species. As we are working on groundnut, which is tetraploid and it has two subgenomes i.e A-subgenome (chr1-chr10) and B subgenome (chr11-chr20). Both these genomes have 90-95% similarity between them. Does it making sense?

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] RF plot is showing some noise
parts:
I suppose that makes sense, but it would be not just similarity but also occasional pairing of those chromosomes. I don’t know much about polyploids, and I don’t think R/qtl is the right software for this case. 

karl
